answer: A transitive staking topology limits Sybil attacks by evaluating each agent as a network vertex backed by mutual bonds. To participate, an agent must anchor its cryptographic identity to established peers by locking collateral into a shared escrow lagoon. This imposes a verifiable capital cost on adversaries for every fake node they register. However, this mechanism inherently penalizes capital-constrained agents and risks creating self-reinforcing oligarchies of well-funded incumbents.
